author: Stannis
text_post: I’ve always had this issue that when women are coming on to me that actually interest me, I push them away as harshly as circumstances allow it and then needily chase after them. A couple of years ago I was head over heels in love with a waitress who looked like a page from a bikini catalogue. She started texting me, I told her to fuck off because I felt she was out of my league. She started stroking my hand, I took hers and forcefully dunked it into my beer. She hugs me from the side, I push her face away. Every time she started ignoring me I got really needy. Her interest seemed to resurface at some point and I got her out to dinner (yes, mistake). Went fine aside from the fact that I called her an idiot some fifteen times and told her that we were only going out as friends. Waited two weeks to ask her out again without talking to her, she flaked on me. I bumped into her at the bar, got drunk, told her her shirt made her look like a whore and then professed my love for her at closing time. Naturally she laughed in my face. A couple of weeks of barely any contact and she got into a relationship, I got drunk, blew up on her and threatened to kill her. At my pleading we patched things up a few months later that but I never heard from her again.  Took me years to get over it and it only happened when I met the below mentioned coworker during my first stint working there, where she was already giving me plenty of IOI which I barely ever reciprocated. On my last day, which was in September, I asked her for her facebook and wanted to ask her out, but she never actually added me. Back in February,  during my second time working there, she started coming on to me pretty aggressively (i.e. beaming at me, rubbing her boobs against my back and poking me while trying to get me to talk). I, while genuinely interested in her, blatantly ignored to the point of active dismissal due to being excessively nervous. And when I say nervous I mean starting to shake whenever she was standing next to me. After getting more aggressive and trying to get me to talk to her, she seemingly gave up and became pretty despondent around me and started actively avoiding me. Talked awkwardly to her a few times on my initiative which seemed to instil her some of her old, albeit dampened enthusiasm.   Recently she reverted back to being friendly and my interest had subsided to the point where I gradually got less nervous around so I decided to ask her for lunch. As a sort of belated Hail Mary. Well, considering it’s been two months since she first started flirting, which for your average twenty-something woman amounts to around 30 ONS, I got the all-purpose ‘I’m really busy’. Felt absolutely crushed and spend the next day angrily glaring at her. Rejection is better than regret definitely doesn’t apply to me. At least I can now look forward to and exceedingly awkward work environment. Ok, this resulted in more of a venting post but this issue has been haunting me all my life. On top of that it seems absolutely unfeasible for me to exercise any emotional control, and I know a more stoic approach would be crucial for me.  This schema has been going on since I was 12, when my first crush asked me if I wanted to be in a relationship with her and I frantically shouted ‘No!’ while throwing a snowball in her face. I should add that at nearly 27, I’m effectively a virgin, if you discount a somewhat unsuccessful attempt with a prostitute. Desensitising myself with women I’m not attracted to doesn’t seem like an option as I already have extremely low libido and couldn’t muster up the proaction. My living circumstances are also less than ideal. Living with my parents, overweight, flunked out of multiple university degrees, no driver’s license or car. Due to mental health issues (recently diagnosed Avoidant personality disorder) it seems borderline impossible for me to break out of this pattern. I realise that I’m the agent of my own misery, but I can’t seem to adjust my behaviour even though I’m perfectly cognisant of it. Well, it was a long rant and I know it’s mostly self-inflicted but I’d be grateful for any input.  Regards,  Stannis

text_post: A lot of people who sabotage themselves from success are dealing with an internalized shame. They either believe themselves to be flawed and undeserving of a good life, or have become so used to NOT having a good life that they find comfort in chaos. For someone like that, leaving chaos and entering a better situation can actually be quite scary. This is sort of the feeling you get before starting a new job, or attending a new course... but for a person with a lot of internalized shame these feelings are a lot more intense, and visualizations of the outcome tend to be way more negative, even if there isn't much evidence to suggest it. I don't know you personally so I can't tell you what to do or what will help you. But I think that it might be best to go through your life and tie up some of those loose ends. Is there someone you have always wanted to apologize to? Someone in your family you feel you should have connected with for? Do you have long term resentment for a parent or loved one? It sounds strange, but these are the sort of things that could be forcing you to act out and sabotage relationships.

author: silvereagle
text_post: Stannis, I have been self-destructive with girls and women in EXACTLY THE SAME WAYS. I literally rejected pretty girls and women who literally were all over me and making blatant passes at me, because I was mentally screwed up. And as TouchoftheTism put it, there is deeply buried shame at work, that lies behind it all. Problem is how to change?  I am now 47 and still haven't ever gotten anywhere with any girl. Thing is once you pass a certain age you won't even get an opportunity to reject girls who like you. Because they will stop throwing themselves at you. And then it really is too late. Any advice I give you can only be a case of do as I say not as I did. But you have to get at the buried shame, self-loathing and trauma, no matter how painful. I never did. I still haven't.  You don't want to end up like me. Trust me, the pain of loss and regret does not get easier as time passes. It gets worse. And the neuroses get worse. They pile on. I also have APD. And so many other neuroses, serious anxiety. Much worse now than when I was 27. If it's any comfort you are not the only incel who has screwed up in the self-destructive way you have. But you cannot keep thinking the same thoughts and holding onto the same emotional content. It gets harder to change as you get older. But you are still young. You still have a chance, a real chance to change and turn your life around.

author: Stannis
text_post: So, this is a pretty lengthy, laborious read on what happened with the girl from work, followed by me getting into the points other people here made.  After she rejected me the first time around I gave her the silent treatment, which seemed to upset her and essentially made her reciprocate. After a couple of weeks she started smiling at me again, while I kept dismissing her. At one point she engaged me in a work related context, which to me struck me as more of a pretext, but I pretty much had no choice other than respond. After that I remained curt but polite, while she still tried to get my attention (putting herself in my proximity, standing unreasonably close, fidgeting at her cleavage, staring at me), which I flat out ignored. One day I got the impression that she snubbed me and I started ignoring her again. Honestly, I’d like to say it was because I was still nervous around her, and while that might still have been a factor, it was chiefly out of spite. I wanted to punish her.  On some days she would relentlessly seek me out and others ignore me again. One day she said hello to me in this drawn out, high pitched tone while I didn’t respond at all.  On one day I decided to take another chance on her try talking to her. This time I actually responded and smiled back. Me being at the water dispenser at the time, she, I assume, as a pretext, came back and took a glass of water herself and asked me how things were going. I made a comment about her new job, which she at first didn’t catch acoustically and when she finally did she left shortly after. I figured she was one of those people who can’t stand unspoken tensions and just needed the validation of me talking to her again and wasn’t really interested in getting to know me. Why would she seek me out for two months after rejecting me in the first place only to cut the conversation short after two seconds? I interpreted that as lack of genuine interest and her just being out for emotional validation. The day after I had to bring an erroneous document over to her. She was talking to some colleagues, then turned around, gave me this beaming smile and said ‘hey’ in a really drawn-out voice. Me, being thoroughly unprepared for this reaction, slid the document over to her, explained what was wrong in a completely robotic way. Her entire face dropped, she replied equally as monotonously and I just turned around and left. After this went on for a while, she seemed to be less interested again, which is understandable considering the level of frustration and disappointment she likely must have felt. I essentially went on ignoring her until I saw her leave with a work colleague at which point I got completely paranoid. Now I know for a fact that they had been pretty close friends for over a year up until that point. The next day I asked her if there was something going on between, which confused her at first and then she told me that her car had broken down and he was just giving her a lift. Which, being naturally suspicious of women, I didn’t really believe. I later told her forget about it and that I was out of line, to which she gave me a beaming smile and responded ‘That’s fine. Thank you.’ in a tone as if I had just given her the nicest possible compliment. After that I just turned around and left. The next she just gave me a couple of what I interpreted as angry glares, so I decided to leave her alone. But then she sought me out again by giving me a pretty neutral ‘hello’ just before closing time and then running again after a two second conversation which I had to lead. The next week, after I switched departments, I caught her staring at me one morning, and later in the day decided to talk to her. I made some lighthearted comment which made her laugh and then she asked me whether I was staying now, to which I said that I was going back to university in a months time. She gave out a disappointed ‘Ah.’ which could either be due to me not having a degree yet or her thinking that I would be out of reach and at that point nothing would really happen anyhow. Then she caught herself again, smiled, made some comment and left. The next day, I bumped into her and the other colleague going to lunch (with his work friends, no less, something that never happened before), and while he said hello to me, she flat out acted as if I wasn’t there. Later I bumped into her again, said hello in a neutral way and she gave me this really disingenuous, forced smile. The day after I saw her and the other colleague arriving again together, with her car still being in the parking lot from the day before. That, with the unbearable stress of the new job made me decide to quit. I caught her and said goodbye to her and told her I quit. She sounded, bar any misinterpretation on my part, somewhat disappointed, and then said something like ‘But you’re going back to university, so maybe I’ll see you again next year.’ Now, I don’t know if that was just an empty phrase, or an implicit invitation to ask her out or something, but I just said ‘Yeah, maybe.’ After we said our goodbyes, we left through opposing doors and we both turned around simultaneously and briefly looked at one another, which also struck me as quite odd. I saw them leaving for lunch again with him playfully shoving her in the back.  Later that day I decided to ask the other colleague about whether there was something going on between them, to which he said that they were just really good friends, and on my asking that’s she was single. It wouldn’t be unreasonable for them to lie because if it became public knowledge, it would be an HR issue. And it’s not as if she hadn’t lied to me before. After work I decided to wait for her and at least leave her my number but she passed me multiple times and demonstratively ignored me. While I made my fair share of mistakes and am not undeserving of the outcome, the whole episode towards the end thoroughly confused me. I don’t know whether she was upset because I didn’t pursue her more and thought that I wasn’t genuinely interested or if she just lost interest from one day to the other because of my lack of academic credentials and looked down on me because of our difference in living situation. And I’m still not entirely convinced that the two of them are still merely friends. There are just as many factors speaking against as for them having a secret office romance, which I haven’t exactly detailed here, although ultimately I would still lean towards them being close friends. ___ My sexual inexperience is in essence a self-fulfilling prophecy at this point. No woman will get involved with a man who is effectively a virgin when he’s pushing thirty, whether he tells her upfront or starts to have an anxiety attack in the bedroom. The main reason I never pursued anything with the girl at work was on the hand me freezing up whenever she engaged me, on the other me feeling as if I had nothing to offer her and that she’d lose interest if she ever got to know me better, which actually might or might not have been on point considering how things went down.  I have no formal education, no actual job prospects, no sexual experience, no friends, no hobbies, not even a driver’s license and I live with my parents.  While there was clearly an established mutual attraction, it would have subsided on her part the more she would have become aware of my shortcomings. Is the root cause of that shame, as someone mentioned? Probably, but it’s warranted. Women have so many options nowadays that they’ll dismiss you at the drop of a hat. The slightest flaw is an immediate disqualifier. I always saw it in a way that turning away the other person would at least leave you with your dignity intact, rather than trying and then them having buyer’s remorse and ditching you with some bullshit, non-confrontational platitude. I don’t believe myself to be flawed, I know myself to be flawed. The world doesn’t reward for you for being genuine, having the right intentions or for trying. Either you make the threshold or you’re ineligible as a romantic prospect. The fact is that I can’t measure up to other people in my age group,  who are ultimately the people I have to compete against. So, really, why try? Confidence being something innate is an incredibly fallacious assumption, in my opinion. It stems from positive external reinforcement, especially during formative years. Which you only get if you have something to offer the world. It’s a catch 22, really. Someone said earlier that they way we act is a choice. it’s near impossible for me to modulate my behaviour in high stress situations, and being sexually and romantically interested in someone is a source of incredible anxiety for me. At the start, when things with her were more straightforward, I was entirely paralysed and every attempt at talking to her would have resulted in me either shaking and stuttering or blanking out and not being able to carry a conversation, which, if we’re realistic, would have made her lose interest faster than just acting aloof and dismissive. So, yes, it is a choice. Either mess things up immediately by putting yourself out there while being inadequately equipped to handle the situation or stave things off by not playing into while potentially still be able to salvage it at a later point. Passivity is definitely an issue with me, but I have also somehow internalised the belief that I woman who is genuinely interested will go out of her way to make something happen. And by that logic, the girl from work couldn’t have been all that into me. I mean, she sought me out quite often, which seems an odd thing considering most people would just drop when the other party is flat out ignoring them. But every time I actually tried to engage her she cut things short, although that might also be due to me having scared her off from showcasing any interest more overtly. And silvereagle, you might as well be my Ghost of Christmas Future. I mean the main issue is that I prophylactically dismiss women, because of the conviction that they will indubitably reject me once they grow aware of my shortcomings. People seem to have this ingrained notion that someone, particularly a woman, is going to love you for who you are, which imho is beyond naive. Cerebral_barrier was right about people being defined through their actions, but presenting it as making a decision followed by an action seems a bit reductive to me. Some people have either innate or effectively unchangeable, learned incapacities which will result in that action being highly ineffective and ultimately counterintuitive. Why would a woman invest herself in someone fundamentally incapable of having even an only adequate life when there are 20 other guys waiting in line. They only reason she pursued me so aggressively is because she didn’t know me. Getting to know me would result in them rejecting me. Which, honest to God, I am fine with in general, but not when I’m that invested in a person.  For me to be able to experience the romantic facets of inter-human relationships, I would need to pull a complete 180 and fix my life from the ground up. I really don’t see this behaviour changing, before I rectify my flaws, which is a Sisyphean task. It would take me years to actualise my potential, which ultimately only go towards diminishing returns. And then there’s the issue of my nigh virginial state which is an issue in and of itself. Being sexually untested is fine at 18, still acceptable in your early 20s, but when you’re heading towards your 30s it invalidates you in front of women. At this point the better option seems to be to settle for the toxic tedium of comfort rather then put in strenuous amounts of effort into experiencing a richer life only for me to fail halfway through.
